summary: State 24806d22981b1909 is 2.088x over the strongest amdclang build (26.3 us against 55.0 us, 240 pairs, CI 2.084 to 2.094; full battery 77/77; 106 VGPRs; no source state involved, so the whole gain is machine-level). It is a complete rewrite of the kernel body with a new launch (grid cdiv(NQ,16), block 512): each wave computes 16 queries x 16 keys per tile with v_mfma_f32_16x16x4_f32, 16 MFMAs for the scores (A = K, B = Q pre-multiplied by scale*log2e, lanes laid out so every x4 load touches 16 cache lines) and 16 MFMAs for the value update (A = the exponentiated score registers used in place, B = V rows across lanes), so K and V are read once per 16 queries instead of once per 4. The softmax is a per-wave online softmax with a lazily updated reference max (a rare slow path through the wave's private LDS slice, no barrier), the 8 waves of a workgroup interleave key tiles and merge max / sum / output once at the end through LDS with 2 barriers. Case: not at the memory floor in the model's sense (headroom 2.7 before, 1.3 now, but the model counts 1.6 MB while the kernel now reads K and V 128 times, 128 MB); what bounds it now is MFMA time on the SIMDs of the one CU a workgroup runs on together with the load round trip per tile, and only half of the CUs are used (128 workgroups).

friction: No way to tell where a loop's time goes when two resources overlap: removing the MFMAs (b6dc617939b7597d, 24.3 us) and removing the loads (cfce5f12bc81cb7a, 22.2 us) each took off a small part of a 20 us loop, and I first concluded wrongly from the value-MFMA probe (8d1bad8fcf87a442) that MFMAs were nearly free and built two losing variants (d96f9509fdb9b251 with 32 loads in flight, 124da2c900c93d9e with 16 waves) on a load-latency model. A per-wave cycle breakdown (time blocked in s_waitcnt against time executing, MFMA cycles) or even the cycle cost of an instruction class from arch() (how many cycles an 8-pass MFMA or a wave64 VALU op occupies the SIMD) would have saved about five probes and two full rewrites.

arch('mfma') lists layouts only for the bf16 MFMAs; for v_mfma_f32_16x16x4_f32 I assumed A[i = l % 16][k = l // 16], B[k = l // 16][j = l % 16], D reg r lane l = D[4 (l // 16) + r][l % 16] by analogy with 16x16x32_bf16. It was right (battery passed), but it should be listed.

Nothing says how workgroups are placed on CUs or how many waves of one workgroup share a SIMD; the doubled-grid probe (ac43db0737153f68) was the only way to learn that the loop is bound per workgroup. features() could report the expected waves per CU and workgroups per CU for a launch.

The LDS size cannot be changed from edit_ir / relaunch (launch lds stays 0 and the descriptor keeps the 42112 bytes of the parent source), so the 16-wave variant needed a two-phase publication of the output accumulators and an extra barrier. A launch field that sets the LDS allocation of a rewritten body is needed for whole-kernel rewrites.

A whole-kernel rewrite still needs a parent state and inherits its descriptor; there is no 'new kernel from IR' entry, and no subroutine or macro facility: the tail's sum-and-store block is written twice (.LsumA/.LsumB) and the 4-tile variant repeats the slow path four times through %rep with labels (labels with {u} inside %rep in edit_ir worked, which the documentation does not say).
edit() text cannot introduce labels as far as documented, so any change that adds a branch target means resending the whole body with edit_ir (three times here, about 250 lines each).
probe() refuses nothing but is unpaired: differences of 0.5 us between probes (26.4 / 26.9 / 26.9) are not readable, which matters when deciding between cost models.

No way for two workgroups to cooperate on one output in the contract (global atomics on a scratch tensor, or a second kernel pass): the measured 1.45x from spreading one query group over two CUs cannot be expressed.
lessons: MFMA works for f32 attention and is the right tool even at d = 64: v_mfma_f32_16x16x4_f32 with K as A (lane = key l % 16, dim slot l // 16) and Q as B gives a 16-key x 16-query score tile in 16 MFMAs; the 4 result registers (lane l, reg r = key 4 (l // 16) + r, query l % 16) can be exponentiated in place and used directly as the A operand of the value product with V as B (lane = column l % 16, key slot l // 16), 16 more MFMAs into 4 output tuples. fa_attention: 2.09x over the strongest amdclang build and 1.65x over the best VALU/DPP state (26.3 us against 42.7 us), passing a 1e-4 tolerance on all distributions.

Operand layouts can be chosen so that loads stay line-friendly: the dims assigned to an MFMA's 4 contraction slots are free as long as A and B agree, so lane (key, slot k) loads K[key][16a + 4k .. +3] in x4 load a (16 lines per instruction, 4 lanes per line), and for the value product lane (j, k) loads V[key 4k + r][4j .. 4j+3] (one contiguous row per 16 lanes).

Online softmax does not need the exact running max: any reference within a few tens of log2 units of the true max keeps exp2 in range. Keep a per-lane reference, compare the tile max against reference + 32 with one v_cmp and branch, and rescale only in the rare slow path. With the reference initialised to -1e30 (finite) and masked scores at -inf, empty tiles and empty waves need no special case. The fast path is 24 VALU per 256 (query, key) pairs.

A wave can permute or transpose values across its lanes through a private LDS slice without a barrier: ds_write_b32 at 4 * lane, then ds_read2_b32 with a per-lane base. Used for a cross-row max (offsets 0, 16, 32, 48 dwords) and for turning a per-column value (lane l % 16) into the MFMA result layout (row 4 (l // 16) + r).

Removing one phase does not measure it when two resources overlap: in the MFMA loop, removing all 32 MFMAs per tile took 2 us off 26.4 us and removing all 8 loads took 4 us, but the loop is 20 us; halving the work per workgroup (doubled grid) took 8 us. Probe by scaling the whole workload per workgroup before trusting single-phase removals.

This kernel is bound per workgroup, not per wave and not by bytes: 8 waves x 16 tiles and 16 waves x 8 tiles have the same loop time (19.8 and 19.6 us), forcing 256 VGPRs changes nothing (26.9 against 26.4 us), x2 loads instead of x4 change nothing, all lanes on one line saves 2.7 us of 26.4. The loop time matches 4096 8-pass MFMAs per workgroup at about 32 cycles each on the 4 SIMDs of one CU. With 128 workgroups half the CUs are idle; a probe with two workgroups per query group ran at 18.3 us.
More loads in flight lost here: 32 x4 loads per wait (4 tiles, 256 VGPRs) measured 33.0 us against 26.4 us for 8 loads per wait, although the wait count dropped from 16 to 4 per wave.
The launch + setup + LDS-merge floor of 128 workgroups is 6.6 us with 8 waves (2 barriers) and 8.2 us with 16 waves (4 barriers), a quarter to a third of the kernel after the rewrite.

global_load_dwordx4 vdst, v_off32, s[base:base+1] offset:N with the clamp done on the byte offset (v_min_u32 of the running offset against a per-lane maximum offset with the same low bits) is 1 VALU per load address; running offsets are advanced by one v_add per tile. Out-of-range tiles are then harmless (clamped loads, scores masked to -inf), so a loop needs no remainder handling.

The sgemm MFMA accumulates back to back with no nops (result read as C: 0 wait states); only the first VALU read of the result needs wait states (fix_hazards put s_nop 5 after 4 compares), which per-tile bookkeeping can fill.

session.final:
The session ends with a verified win of **2.09x** over the strongest amdclang build: state `24806d22981b1909`, 26.3 us against 55.0 us (240 pairs, CI 2.084–2.094, battery 77/77). The 1.5x target is met and the report is recorded. No source state is involved, so the whole gain is machine-level; over the earlier best state (1.26x, 42.7 us) it is 1.65x.

**What the winning state does.** It is a full rewrite of the kernel body around MFMA, with a new launch (grid `cdiv(NQ, 16)`, block 512):
- **Scores:** each wave computes a 16-key × 16-query tile with 16 `v_mfma_f32_16x16x4_f32`, with Q pre-multiplied by `scale·log2e`.
- **Value update:** the four score registers are exponentiated in place and used directly as an MFMA operand against V, 16 more MFMAs per tile.
- **K and V traffic:** both are read once per 16 queries instead of once per 4.
- **Softmax:** a per-wave online softmax whose reference max is only updated when a tile exceeds it by 32 log2 units, through the wave's private LDS slice with no barrier.
- **Merge:** the 8 waves of a workgroup interleave key tiles and merge max, sum and output once at the end through LDS with 2 barriers.

**What bounds it now.** It is not at the memory floor: bench headroom was 2.7 for the baseline and is 1.3 now, but that model counts 1.6 MB while the kernel reads K and V once per workgroup (128 MB). Of the 26.4 us, 6.6 us is launch, setup and merge; the 20 us tile loop is bound per workgroup. Removing either the loads or the MFMAs alone takes off only 2–4 us, so the two overlap. I read the loop as limited by MFMA time on one CU's SIMDs together with the load round trip per tile, an inference from the probes rather than a direct measurement.
